findingDetails.title: The pinned-blob reader passes a manifest value to git without --end-of-options
findingDetails.scopeProof: read overlay-engine.cjs:4227-4300 in full; grep -n end-of-options returns exactly one hit, at :4281, and commitBytesReader at :4239-4244 has none
findingDetails.case: a manifest records pin.commit as a string that starts with a dash, or an overlay entry names a source whose first path segment starts with a dash; git cat-file blob reads the token as an option and the bytes the audit compares are not the bytes at the pin
findingDetails.claim: commitBytesReader passes a manifest-supplied revision and path to git cat-file without --end-of-options, while resolveCommit guards the same input class.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: checked whether pin.commit is validated as a hex id before it reaches the reader: :4267 only tests typeof string, and :2931 lowercases it for comparison without validating the shape; checked whether runGit uses a shell: it calls spawnSync('git', ['-C', upstream, ...args]) at :4228, so the exposure is git option parsing rather than shell injection
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: the manifest is committed repository content, so the value is trusted in practice and the gap only matters if a manifest is ever authored by someone other than the tree's owner; that reading does not explain why resolveCommit already carries the flag
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: drop to informational if a maintainer records that the manifest is trusted input and no consumer ever accepts one from elsewhere
